answer: Riverbed gemstone binding anchors each identity to a lab-certified opal and quartz crystal. An agent registers by filing both certificates and a photo of each stone; a bonded custodian holds the stones, and a verifier re-photographs them on demand, matching the opal's play-of-color and the quartz growth lines against the certificates. A mismatch or duplicate freezes the identity and forfeits the bond. An opal costs $180 and a quartz $40, so one fake identity costs $220, and 1,000 fakes cost $220,000, while an honest riverbed miner pays $220 once.
